Retail demand for Anthropic is accelerating:

Retail investors bought +$100 million in Anthropic, $ANT, shares on Monday, marking a 2nd consecutive daily increase in purchases.

As a result, $ANT was the 2nd-most purchased stock among retail investors during that session.

That compares to +$60 million on Thursday, Anthropic's IPO day, the 3rd-largest retail purchase on the first trading day of any IPO since 2018.

Only SpaceX, $SPCX, in June 2026, at +$118 million, and Coinbase, $COIN, in April 2021, at +$92 million, recorded larger retail purchases on their respective IPO days.

In total, retail investors purchased +$252 million in Anthropic shares over 3 trading days ending Monday.

Retail is piling into $ANT.

Based on the consensus estimates for the next 5 quarters (from BBG), the trajectory form here is for the 5-year earnings CAGR to remain elevated in the low double digits. This tells me that earnings estimate revisions will be a key driver as we head into 2027.

The Bitcoin chart looks weak.

The bears and short-term traders have an increasingly convincing case for more downside.

There’s no two ways about it. I’ve been feeling pretty bearish. But this is the beauty of the sentiment data. We can use these tools to analyze our own emotional thinking and give ourselves a more logical way to think about the market we currently find ourselves in.

How much do we let the crowd influence our thinking?

When should we fade our own emotionality?

These are challenging questions we'll explore today.

Fear and boredom can eventually push people toward that big red sell button. And while you’re making that decision, it can feel perfectly rational (I’m as susceptible to these feeling as anyone).

That’s why I keep coming back to this process.

This week, I put my own reaction against the data and walk you through where I land, including what I’m still uncertain about.

In today’s Sentiment Scan, I’ll show you which parts of the bearish case I find convincing, how I weigh them against the longer-term evidence, and what the different communities are telling me about the Bitcoin price.

BREAKING: US October PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred inflation metric, rises to 3.8%, its 2nd-highest level since April 2023.

Core PCE inflation also rose to 3.3%, above expectations of 3.2%.

CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation all continue to push higher.

December rate hike odds are rising.

The valuation question remains central to this market cycle. Investors haven’t been paying up for those lofty earnings estimates, and that’s likely for three reasons. One, investors usually don’t pay peak multiples for peak earnings growth. Earnings are cyclical, after all. Second, with cashflows being spent on capex instead of buybacks, investors have less to show for those earnings in the form of a robust payout ratio. And third, financial conditions are inversely correlated to P/E multiples, and those conditions have been tightening as both short and long yields remain in uptrends, the dollar is bid, and credit spreads have widened.

➡️“autopilot on hikes” and 2026 “get inflation down to 2%”
➡️midterm election year, Dems gain
➡️stocks already down -10%

One notable difference, for me, is that as markets looked ahead, there was no obvious positive driver:

➡️in 2018, there was no AI story
➡️in 2018, the 2017 tax cuts boost was fading
➡️in 2018, into the Fall, there was no “big trade”

By comparsion today, we are witnessing a “supply shock” to the AI story:

➡️AI policy risk from governers, “supply shock”
➡️debt markets cautious, “supply shock”
➡️ Fed risk “supply shock”
➡️Demand for AI strong
➡️AI discovery strong
➡️Physical AI ahead

2018 created “end cycle” risk
2026 is when will “shocks pass”

To us, this is why we see less downside into year-end.
